openwrt_commit.nachricht:
ramips: add support for D-Link DAP-X1860 A1

The DAP-X1860 is a wall-plug AX1800 repeater.

Specifications:
- MT7621, 256 MiB RAM, 128 MiB SPI NAND
- MT7915 + MT7975 2x2 802.11ax (DBDC)
- Ethernet: 1 port 10/100/1000
- LED RSSI bargraph (2x green, 1x red/orange), status
  and RSSI LEDs are incorrectly populated red/orange
  (should be red/green according to documentation)

Installation:
- Keep reset button pressed during plug-in
- Web Recovery Updater is at 192.168.0.50
- Upload factory.bin, confirm flashing
  (seems to work best with Chromium-based browsers)

Revert to OEM firmware:
- tar -xvf DAP-X1860_RevA_Firmware_101b94.bin
- openssl enc -d -md md5 -aes-256-cbc -in FWImage.st2 \
  -out FWImage.st1 -k MB0dBx62oXJXDvt12lETWQ==
- tar -xvf FWImage.st1
- flash kernel_DAP-X1860.bin via Recovery

Signed-off-by: Sebastian Schaper <openwrt@sebastianschaper.net>

openwrt_commit_elx.nachricht:
build: fix image headers silently truncated with uutils coreutils

Build/elx-header and Build/znet-header convert a hex string into \xHH
escape sequences using `fold -s2`. This relies on the obsolete -WIDTH
option syntax of GNU fold, which parses "-s2" as "-s -2". uutils
coreutils does not support this syntax and fails with:

  error: unexpected argument '-2' found

    tip: to pass '-2' as a value, use '-- -2'

Since fold writes nothing to stdout in this case, the command
substitution expands to an empty string. The following
`dd bs=N count=1 conv=sync` then writes zero bytes, because conv=sync
only pads partial input blocks and never pads empty input. The header
field is dropped entirely, and all subsequent fields move to lower
offsets.

The build still succeeds, because the failure happens inside the
subshell which is then handed to echo.
The malformed images are only rejected when a device tries to
boot them.

For example, on the Zyxel WSM20, the missing payload size field in the
znet-header moves the 0x12345678 magic and the payload to unexpected
offsets. The bootloader then rejects the image, even though sysupgrade
accepted it.

This affects all builds on Ubuntu 25.10 and later, because these
releases use uutils coreutils by default.

Replace `fold -s2` with `fold -w2`, which is the documented way to set
the line width and produces identical output with GNU fold.

Affected devices:
- Build/znet-header is used in all images of the Zyxel WSM20 and the
  ELECOM WRC-X1800GS
- Build/elx-header is used in the factory images of the ELECOM
  WAB-I1750-PS, WAB-S1167-PS, WAB-S600-PS, WRC-2533GHBK-I and
  WRC-2533GHBK2-T, the I-O DATA WN-AC1167GR, WN-AC733GR3 and WNPR2600G,
  the Edimax RA21S and RG21S, and the D-Link DAP-X1860 A1

Signed-off-by: Grische <github@grische.xyz>
Assisted-by: Claude:claude-opus-5
Link: https://github.com/openwrt/openwrt/pull/25410
Signed-off-by: Hauke Mehrtens <hauke@hauke-m.de>

roh.openwrt_image_mk:
define Device/dlink_dap-x1860-a1
  $(Device/nand)
  IMAGE_SIZE := 53248k
  DEVICE_VENDOR := D-Link
  DEVICE_MODEL := DAP-X1860
  DEVICE_VARIANT := A1
  KERNEL_SIZE := 8192k
  KERNEL_LOADADDR := 0x82000000
  KERNEL := kernel-bin | relocate-kernel $(loadaddr-y) | lzma | \
	fit lzma $$(KDIR)/image-$$(firstword $$(DEVICE_DTS)).dtb
  IMAGES += factory.bin
  IMAGE/factory.bin := append-kernel | pad-to $$(KERNEL_SIZE) | append-ubi | \
	check-size | elx-header 011b0060 8844A2D168B45A2D
  DEVICE_PACKAGES := kmod-mt7915-firmware rssileds -uboot-envtools
endef
TARGET_DEVICES += dlink_dap-x1860-a1

openwrt_forum.#152: 2023-04-02 s_2:  We have all the allvailable LED GPIOs declared in the dts, they are controlled by the MT7621 directly, i.e. not addressable or requiring any separate driver (like e.g. Ubiquiti AirCube devices). Except for the bootup blinking sequence, there is not much default LED behaviour in OpenWrt, except for Ethernet ports or (single band) wireless radios. Since this device has no separate LEDs for 2.4 / 5 GHz, I think there is currently no way of e.g. having a throughput indicator that covers both bands with a single LED. Also that is not what the OEM firmware would do, I think the Power / Status LED is just permanent on in normal operation? What is the expected LED behaviour you would like to see in OpenWrt?

Das gilt meiner Erfahrung nach für alle mediatek filogic devices und leider auch für mt7621+mt7915e. An Standorten an denen weniger los ist, laufen beide targets wiederum sehr gut und dort nutze ich sie aus Preisgründen dann sehr gerne. Leider kann ich keinen eindeutigen Auslöser feststellen, deswegen nutze ich mal die schwammige Formulierung „nicht stressfest“. In der Innenstadt direkt am Fenster in Mietshaus Häuserfluchten(Viele andere APs und clients) an viel befahrener Straße(weitere clients die sich rasch connecten und disconnecten sowie wifi APs von Autos) ist filogic einfach instabil und unnutzbar. Für stressige Umgebungen nutze ich lieber Ipq40xx wie die Fritzbox 7520, oder Geräte wie den Extreme Networks WS-AP3825i aus dem mpc85xx-p1020 target. Andere Geräte des zweiten targets kenne ich aber nicht. Zu wenig Erfahrung um eine Aussage zu treffen habe ich mit mt7622, da wäre mal interessant ob das stabil läuft unter Stress. Meine oben beschrieben Erfahrungen verallgemeinere ich auf gesamte targets, obwohl ich jeweils nur 3-5 Geräte des targets getestet habe, es muss also nicht wirklich das gesamte target betroffen sein, ich halte es nur für wahrscheinlich. Gefühlt ist es über die Zeit wesentlich besser geworden, nur unter starkem Stress stabil sind sie halt immernoch nicht.

Widersprueche: SPI-NAND (Commit) vs. paralleles MX30LF1G18AC; hwdata-Strom "12 VDC 2.0A via barrel" vs. Netzstecker; Reset Seite vs. Unterseite (QIG); 293 vs. 284 g; 3- vs. 4-stufige Signal-LED; Recovery-LED orange vs. rot blinkend.
